title: Consolidate SDK locking and strip legacy compatibility layer
creator: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Across Python/JS/Go SDKs we've accumulated multiple ad-hoc lockfiles and a lightweight compatibility shim that maps old API params to the new surface. The shim increases maintenance burden, prevents removal of dead code, and hides real dependency conflicts. This ticket coordinates a cross-language effort to (1) adopt a clearer locked-dependency policy and canonicalize lock artifacts, (2) bump critical runtime and networking libraries to supported versions, and (3) remove the legacy compatibility layer and deprecated request fields after staged rollouts and client migrations. Outcome: slimmer SDK bundles, fewer runtime edge-case patches, and measurable latency/stability gains when combined with runtime improvements.
background: We introduced the compatibility shim in 2023 to preserve backwards compatibility for customers using older client fields (e.g., old 'model' aliases and deprecated transport flags). Recent telemetry shows the shim is exercised in <2% of requests but adds nontrivial branching and serialization overhead in the client code paths. Concurrently, dependency drift across language clients has caused occasional CI flakiness and security alerts (outdated http libs, transitive protobufs). Prior attempts to bump deps independently resulted in divergent lockfiles and multiple hotfixes. We now need a coordinated, auditable upgrade with migration docs and a short deprecation window.
acceptance_criteria: Root-level canonical lock manifest defined and committed for each language (pyproject.lock / package-lock.json OR yarn.lock policy documented)
Python: bump httpx>=0.24, attrs>=23.2, and pinned urllib3 resolved; run full unit + integration suite in py3.10-3.12 matrix
JavaScript: bump axios>=1.5, typescript>=5.3, and ensure Node 18+ compatibility; update bundling to esbuild 0.20+ for smaller bundles
Go: upgrade go.mod to require go 1.21 (or current LTS), update grpc/protobuf transitive pins and regenerate clients
Compatibility shim removed from all 3 SDKs with a migration guide and deprecation notice published
Performance: client cold-start median reduced by >=6% in microbench harness for typical chat/generate calls
No high-severity security advisories in dependency tree after bump (scan reports clean)
Canary rollout completed and no critical regressions after 72 hours
tasks: Audit transitive deps and produce per-language dependency matrix
Define canonical lockfile policy and commit governance doc to /docs/sdk-locking.md
Implement lock consolidation PRs in python/, js/, go/ subrepos and enable CI job to verify locks are in sync
Bump network and serialization libs, run compatibility test harness
Remove compatibility shim and deprecated request fields from SDK input validation layers
Publish migration guide and changelog entries with code examples for common upgrade patterns
Coordinate canary release across Hosted API clients and observe telemetry for 7 days
Prepare rollback PRs and automated feature-flag toggles for fast revert
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Initial audit completed. Identified four transitive protobuf versions across SDKs and two critical http libs that require bumps.
2026-02-28: Governance doc proposal posted: /docs/sdk-locking.md (link below). Team consensus around adopting language-specific lockfiles but single-source audit manifest in repo root.
2026-03-03: Python dependency PR created (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/422). Bumped httpx->0.24.1 and removed urllib3 direct pin where redundant.
2026-03-05: JS PR opened (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/801). Bumped axios->1.5.2, typescript->5.3.4 and updated esbuild to 0.20.8; bundle size reduced ~8% in local checks.
2026-03-08: Go PR under review (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/210). go.mod updated to go 1.21 and regenerated protobuf client stubs.
2026-03-10: Compatibility shim removal branch ready for internal review (python: branch compat/strip-shim). Running integration tests against canary runtime to validate behavior.
risks: Removing the shim may cause breakage for a small set of customers that rely on deprecated alias fields — need clear communication and targeted outreach
Dependency bumps could surface subtle behavioral changes (e.g., header normalization, timeout semantics) requiring additional test cases
Binary size regressions in JS/Go if transitive deps are not deduped properly; must validate bundle and module sizes
Coordinating simultaneous releases across three language clients increases release coordination complexity and potential for release window drift
test_plan: Unit + integration suites across Python 3.10/3.11/3.12, Node 18/20, Go 1.21 in CI matrix
Contract tests against the hosted API mock to ensure request shapes unchanged except for removed deprecated fields
Performance microbench: generate/chat baseline vs post-change for cold and warm cache scenarios
Security scan of dependency trees using Snyk and internal tooling; remediate any medium/high findings before merge
Canary deployment: roll out 5% of SDK traffic for 72 hours, then 25%, then 100% after validation
migration_notes: Provide code snippets in Python and JS for mapping old field names to new ones; link to migration doc in docs/clients/migration-2026-03.md
Recommend customers pin to the previous SDK minor for emergency rollback; provide support escalation path with template PR for customers needing more time
rollback_plan: Re-enable compatibility shim behind feature-flag if regression observed
Revert language-specific dependency PRs and publish emergency patch clients on previous minor
Notify customers via status page and targeted emails with rollback instructions
notes: Target date for public SDK release: 2026-03-20 (dependent on canary results)
Coordinate with docs and developer advocacy for blog post and migration walkthroughs
